summary: Anchored action menu with flat commands, grouped sections, single-selection choices, supplemental notification dots or trailing tags, prefix icons, reorderable rows, switches, independent trailing actions, separate trailing toggles, and destructive actions.
useWhen: A trigger reveals a short contextual list of commands or state-changing actions.
Actions need grouping, mutually exclusive selected state, supplemental notification dots or trailing tags, prefix icons, reorderable switch or command rows, or destructive treatment.
avoidWhen: The user is selecting a value for a form field.
The content requires rich dialog interaction or a multi-step workflow.
The actions should remain persistently visible.

alternatives.when: The choice is a form value with a label, validation, and submitted value.
alternatives.reason: Select provides form-control semantics and value ownership.

alternatives.when: Several form values may be selected.
alternatives.reason: Select multiple provides multi-select listbox semantics, array value ownership, and count presentation.

alternatives.when: The interaction needs substantial content, confirmation, or a form.
alternatives.reason: Modal owns focus containment and dialog-level interaction.

accessibility: An empty choice collection can show informational copy in a focusable non-modal dialog instead of rendering a fake disabled action. Escape and Tab retain the normal popup dismissal and anchor-focus behavior.
Anchor the menu to the control that opens it and return focus to that control when the menu closes.
Open with visible initial focus only when the trigger was activated from the keyboard.
Keep disabled items discoverable only when their unavailable state is meaningful.
Switch rows use menuitemcheckbox semantics on the row; the nested ds-switch is an aria-hidden presentation indicator at the same density as the menu.
Single-selection menus use menuitemradio semantics and aria-checked on each row, but render no nested radio control; selected interaction fill and primary foreground provide the visual state.

A swatch-picker section changes the popup to a non-modal dialog so its radio group and ordinary preference buttons keep valid nested semantics; Tab moves between its controls, then leaves and closes at the popup boundary.
When the anchor is inside an open shadow tree, pass its HTMLElement through anchor. Outside activation, focus return, and forward Tab continuation follow the composed tree across that boundary.
Use notification dots only as supplemental status and not as the sole indication of important information.
Trailing tags are non-interactive supplemental content; their visible label remains part of the menu item's accessible name.

Reorderable rows keep a presentation Drag handle. Pointer drag on the handle and Alt+Arrow Up or Down emit dsReorder without closing. Pointer cancellation abandons the pending move. Hide-locked reorderable rows expose aria-disabled for the unavailable toggle but stay focusable so they can move; fully locked rows stay out of the contiguous reorderable run. Use reorderHandleInactive to retain quaternary Drag dots without exposing drag interaction when a temporarily fixed row still needs visual alignment.

A row may append one separately focusable icon toggle after a decorative tertiary divider. The popup uses non-modal dialog semantics for this composite content, the row retains its primary command or visibility toggle, and dsItemToggle reports the requested controlled state without closing the surface.

A composite row may expose independent trailing icon actions without making its non-actionable row surface appear clickable. Active Drag handles and trailing actions own separate inset hover and pressed feedback. Each action has its own accessible name, does not use aria-pressed, and reports its stable action identity through dsItemToggle without closing the surface.
Announce the new position through a polite live region that is a sibling of the role=menu popup, so the menu retains only permitted descendants.
states: The host owns open state and responds to selection and close events.
Use either flat items or sections, not both.
After dsSelect from a switch row, replace the items or sections array with updated switchValue data so the controlled indicator reflects the new state.
After dsReorder, replace items or the affected section with the emitted items array. Menu never mutates order and does not close.
For selectionMode single, keep exactly one item isSelected and replace the items or sections array after dsSelect; Menu never mutates consumer-owned selection data.
Arrays, objects, and element anchors must be assigned as JavaScript properties.
anchorId resolves only in the document tree; use the anchor property for a trigger rendered inside a shadow root.
Use a swatch-picker section for a small curated visual preference and apply dsSwatchSelect immediately without closing the popup.
Ordinary rows, section headings, and supporting text consume the Menu size. At xs, both the primary label and supporting text use caption metrics.
A trailing tag resolves one density smaller than its menu row and uses the inset recipe so it nests without changing row height. Do not combine tag, dot, and switch suffixes on one item.

Reorderable rows use the Drag prefix and ignore icon. Active drag handles inherit the choice-popup secondary foreground; inactive drag handles use quaternary foreground. When any row in a section has an icon, an active handle, or an inactive handle, the remaining rows get a spacer so labels align.
Embedded mode renders the same controlled content inside a parent-owned surface; the parent owns positioning, initial focus, Escape, Tab exit, and dismissal.
responsiveBehavior: Keep the default choice-cell anchor alignment so the first or last interactive row edge aligns with its trigger, matching Select; use popup-frame only for deliberate custom frame geometry.

Treat side as the preferred placement. When the popup cannot fit there and the opposite side offers more room, Menu flips on that main axis before clamping to the nearest data-ds-overlay-boundary rectangle or the viewport fallback.
Keep the popup attached while its external anchor moves or resizes, including during CSS transitions in responsive shell chrome.
Cap the popup to the vertical room available on its resolved side. When content is taller, the choice list scrolls internally and keyboard focus scrolls the active row into view.
Assign boundary as an HTMLElement only when the nearest composed-tree boundary is not the intended collision owner.
Avoid fixed widths that exceed narrow collision boundaries.

customElements: Assign items, sections, and HTMLElement anchors as properties after the element is defined.

Handle dsReorder by replacing the items or section items with the emitted items array; Menu never mutates order. Handle dsItemToggle by replacing either the controlled trailingToggle state or the requested trailingActions state without changing unrelated row state.
react: Pass arrays and objects as wrapper props and handle generated onDsSelect, onDsItemToggle, onDsReorder, and onDsClose event props.
angular: Use property bindings for arrays, objects, and anchors and event bindings for dsSelect, dsItemToggle, dsReorder, and dsClose.

styling.rationale: The component owns the protected recipes below; unspecified host properties and application layout remain customizable.

protected.reason: The component owns its surface and interaction treatment; use its semantic presentation props or compose an application-owned surrounding surface.
The component owns its surface radius; retain the shared recipe and customize an outer wrapper when needed.
